Forwarding DataCraft's redlines — see attached. Summary / asks for Legal and Sales: 

1) DataCraft is asking for assignment of output/derivative rights when they "productize" features built using DataCraft inputs. They framed this as non-negotiable for procurement.
2) They want a hard prohibition on using their content to retrain Redwood models unless DataCraft signs an opt-in.
3) They also want 12 months of telemetry/audit logs accessible for compliance.

My thoughts: assignment across the board is risky; we should offer a narrower carve (assignment limited to downstream product artifacts created via an explicit productization export path) + preserve ability to improve models with aggregated, anonymized signals unless they opt-out. Also operationally we can offer a 12-month retention window and produce an evidence pack on request (subject to scope/fees).

Laura — can you draft a one-paragraph compromise and a redline snippet for the OF/MSA that we can send back? Keep it tight so procurement can sign quickly.
Priyom — heads-up for the AM and procurement timeline; DataCraft wants Q4 signoff.

Thanks — Raf

Rafael / Priyom,

Thanks for the context. Draft compromise below — intent is to minimize operational risk while addressing DataCraft's procurement needs. Suggested language for the order form (redline snippet):

"If Customer elects the Productization Export (as defined in Exhibit A), Customer shall receive assignment of rights solely in the specific Productized Artifacts created from Customer Content submitted through the Productization Export. For all other Outputs, Redwood grants Customer a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive license to use, reproduce, and distribute Outputs.

Redwood shall not use Customer Content, Customer Outputs, or other Customer-specific data to train, fine-tune, or improve Redwood's foundational or service models without Customer's prior written consent. Redwood may, however, collect and use aggregated, de-identified telemetry and usage metrics for service quality, security, and feature development, provided such data cannot be re-associated with Customer or individual end users.

Redwood will retain request-level audit logs and selectable telemetry for a default period of 90 days. For customers with compliance requirements, Redwood offers extended retention of up to 12 months for a documented evidence pack subject to an agreed fee and data handling procedures outlined in Exhibit B."

Operational notes: 
- Assigning only productized artifacts avoids blanket assignment risk.
- The opt-in for model training satisfies their prohibition ask while preserving our R&D ability via de-identified aggregates.
- 12 months retention is reasonable if we scope it as a paid compliance add-on; this protects operational cost and security posture.

If you want, I can attach a PDF redline and a suggested Exhibit B scope. Also recommend adding a fallback clause: if customer requests auditor access or forensic analysis, we handle per an approved engagement and confidentiality terms.

If everyone agrees, I can draft the OF redline and a short cover email for Susan.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Proposed compromise: Productization assignment + training opt-in (DataCraft)

Hi Susan / Evan / Procurement team,

Thanks for the redlines and for being candid about procurement timelines. Redwood wants to be helpful and move this forward quickly. Per internal legal and product review, we propose the following compromise (summary + attached redline):

1) Assignment limited to Productized Artifacts: If DataCraft elects the Productization Export defined in Exhibit A, DataCraft will receive assignment of rights in those specific Productized Artifacts only. This keeps assignment narrow and tied to an explicit customer action.

2) Training and model use: Redwood will not use Customer Content or Customer Outputs to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve its foundational or service models without Customer's prior written consent. Redwood retains the right to collect aggregated, de-identified telemetry for service improvement.

3) Audit & retention: Redwood offers a standard 90-day retention for request-level logs. For compliance customers, we can provide a 12-month retention evidence pack (audit logs + sample outputs) as an optional add-on; we can scope handling procedures in Exhibit B. We will provide delivery timelines and any applicable fees in the OF.

4) Operational safeguards: KMS-backed keys for customer secrets (if requested), role-based access to evidence packs, and a documented procedure for forensic requests.

Attached is a redlined OF and a short Exhibit B draft. If this approach is acceptable, we can finalize the order form and route the DocuSign link. If you prefer alternate phrasing, please flag the specific lines and we’ll iterate quickly. 

We want to keep Q4 on track — would you be able to review and confirm if this satisfies DataCraft counsel by EOD Wednesday?

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
